title: Little’s law in a team’s language: work in progress, throughput and lead time

videos.script: Here is a board on an ordinary Tuesday. Sixteen cards are open, and everybody is busy. {{board}} Ask the team when the next card will be done, and you will hear a guess. {{guess}} There is a better answer, and the board already holds it. {{record}} Three numbers describe any team that takes work in and lets it out. How much is open. How fast it leaves. How long each piece stays. {{three}} They are not three facts. They are one fact, written three ways, and John Little proved it in 1961. {{law}} Know two of them, and the third is arithmetic. {{arithmetic}} This lesson puts that law into a team's words. Then it sets up the computer you will use for the whole course. {{setup}} You will run a short program that writes four months of one team's history. And you will check the law against it, including the month it fails. {{fails}}
